Single-cell: comparing conditions

Source: vignettes/articles/sc-conditions.Rmd
sc-conditions.Rmd

Question: between two conditions, do the proportions of cell types change, and where on the embedding are cells gained or lost?

Function Use
summarize_group_meta() counts and proportions per group, condition (and sample)
get_meta_pivot() a quick two-way table of two metadata columns
plot_composition_scatter() proportion of each group in one condition against another
DensityDiffPlot_bioToolkit() where on an embedding a condition has more or fewer cells

These plots describe differences; they do not test them. Cells from one sample are not independent replicates, so tests of composition must use samples (e.g. propeller, scCODA, Milo).

Data: 8,000 PBMCs from Kang et al. 2018, 8 donors, each sampled as control and after 6 h of interferon-β (IFN-β): 16 samples.

pbmc <- docs_kang()

Counting cells

summarize_group_meta() counts the cells of each group per condition (and per sample with sample.by) and their proportion of the condition’s cells. It takes a Seurat object or its metadata.

comp <- summarize_group_meta(pbmc, group.by = "cell_type", split.by = "condition")
head(comp)
#>   condition       group count total       prop
#> 1   Control       CD4 T  1666  3957 0.42102603
#> 2   Control       CD8 T   348  3957 0.08794541
#> 3   Control          NK   275  3957 0.06949709
#> 4   Control           B   417  3957 0.10538287
#> 5   Control   CD14 Mono   907  3957 0.22921405
#> 6   Control FCGR3A Mono   228  3957 0.05761941
per_sample <- summarize_group_meta(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    split.by = "condition",
    sample.by = "donor"
)
head(per_sample, 3)
#>   sample condition group count total       prop
#> 1   D101   Control CD4 T    85   287 0.29616725
#> 2   D101   Control CD8 T    23   287 0.08013937
#> 3   D101   Control    NK    21   287 0.07317073

get_meta_pivot() gives a two-way table of any two columns, as counts or as percentages of rows, columns or the total:

get_meta_pivot(pbmc$cell_type, pbmc$condition, type = "count")
#> # A tibble: 8 × 3
#>   row_metadata  Control `IFN-beta`
#>   <fct>           <int>      <int>
#> 1 CD4 T            1666       1753
#> 2 CD8 T             348        310
#> 3 NK                275        337
#> 4 B                 417        387
#> 5 CD14 Mono         907        859
#> 6 FCGR3A Mono       228        284
#> 7 DC                 65         72
#> 8 Megakaryocyte      51         41
get_meta_pivot(
    pbmc$cell_type,
    pbmc$condition,
    type = "percent",
    margin = "column"
)
#> # A tibble: 8 × 3
#>   row_metadata  Control `IFN-beta`
#>   <fct>           <dbl>      <dbl>
#> 1 CD4 T           42.1       43.4 
#> 2 CD8 T            8.79       7.67
#> 3 NK               6.95       8.34
#> 4 B               10.5        9.57
#> 5 CD14 Mono       22.9       21.2 
#> 6 FCGR3A Mono      5.76       7.02
#> 7 DC               1.64       1.78
#> 8 Megakaryocyte    1.29       1.01

Composition scatter

Each group’s proportion in one condition (x) against the other (y), with the y = x line: groups above it are more abundant in the y condition.

plot_composition_scatter(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    split.by = "condition",
    x = "Control",
    y = "IFN-beta"
)

Six hours of IFN-β leave the cell type composition almost unchanged: all cell types lie on the line. The response is a change of state, seen in the expression of interferon-stimulated genes (see Expression across groups).

Variants

Proportions per sample, each point the mean of a condition’s samples, so that every donor counts the same. The horizontal bar is computed from the samples of the x condition and the vertical bar from those of the y condition: error chooses the SEM (default), the SD of the samples, or a 95% confidence interval of the mean ("ci95", mean ± t(0.975, n - 1) × SEM, t-based since there are few samples per condition).

plot_composition_scatter(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    split.by = "condition",
    sample.by = "donor"
)

plot_composition_scatter(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    split.by = "condition",
    sample.by = "donor",
    error = "ci95",
    log = TRUE
)

Log axes spread rare groups; fold.lines = 2 draws y = 2x and y = x / 2:

plot_composition_scatter(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    split.by = "condition",
    log = TRUE,
    fold.lines = 2
)

Numbers of cells instead of proportions:

plot_composition_scatter(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    split.by = "condition",
    value = "count",
    log = TRUE
)

One panel per level of a third column, with proportions computed within each, e.g. within lymphoid and myeloid cells:

is_lymphoid <- pbmc$cell_type %in% c("CD4 T", "CD8 T", "NK", "B")
pbmc$lineage <- factor(
    ifelse(is_lymphoid, "Lymphoid", "Myeloid"),
    levels = c("Lymphoid", "Myeloid")
)
plot_composition_scatter(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    split.by = "condition",
    facet.by = "lineage",
    panel.width = 2.2,
    cells = colnames(pbmc)[pbmc$cell_type != "Megakaryocyte"]
)

Density difference on the embedding

DensityDiffPlot_bioToolkit() estimates the density of cells of each condition on the embedding (normalized, so cell numbers do not matter) and draws the difference from a reference condition: magenta where the compared condition has relatively more cells, blue where it has fewer. The colour scale is centred on 0 and each side reaches its full colour at its own extreme. With sample.by, each sample’s density is computed separately and averaged, so one large sample cannot drive the map.

What the map means depends on the embedding. On the integrated UMAP (Harmony over condition), cells of both conditions are aligned by cell type, so the map shows shifts within cell types:

DensityDiffPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    split.by = "condition",
    reference = "Control",
    sample.by = "sample",
    label = TRUE,
    label.by = "cell_type"
)

On the UMAP before integration, IFN-β-stimulated cells of every type sit apart from their controls, and the map shows that response as a separation:

DensityDiffPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    split.by = "condition",
    reference = "Control",
    sample.by = "sample",
    reduction = "umap.unintegrated",
    label = TRUE,
    label.by = "cell_type"
)

Variants

The log2 ratio of the two densities instead of their difference: fold changes, which also show sparse regions.

DensityDiffPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    split.by = "condition",
    reference = "Control",
    sample.by = "sample",
    measure = "log2ratio"
)

The density difference drawn as a continuous surface, with contours of the density of all cells:

DensityDiffPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    split.by = "condition",
    reference = "Control",
    sample.by = "sample",
    draw = "raster",
    contour = TRUE
)

The bandwidth multiplier: below 1 resolves smaller regions, above 1 smooths more.

DensityDiffPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    split.by = "condition",
    reference = "Control",
    sample.by = "sample",
    density.adjust = 0.5
)
